title: Round 2.3 TM-01 Block.pptx
doc_type: presentation, bid evaluation (text only; images not rendered)
issuer_author: Tonalli / IFR (slides reference "IFR" volumetrics and "gives Tonalli an advantage")
summary: Evaluation of CNH Round 2.3 block TM-01 in the El Abra trend, using Tecolutla as a comparison. Slide titles: Seismic Review of El Abra Reservoir; Fluid Factor Volume; Oil in Place per Field; Recovery Factors; Recent well results; El Abra depth contours to -2,380 m for Tecolutla, Miguel Hidalgo, Miguel Hidalgo-to-Tecolutla, Vicente Guerrero, Gutierrez Zamora; In-situ Vp/Vs reservoir differentiation ("difficult to differentiate oil from gas, both compressible"); brine/oil/gas carbonate vs background Vp-Vs trend; MH-412 synthetic tie to 10-degree angle stack ("fair correlation at ZOI"); AVO fluid-factor (AVOFF) arbitrary line, carbonate trend 5-45 degrees, PSTM gathers; Tecolutla seismic dip line ("Carbonate Reef"); Tecolutla and TM-01 AVO response. Conclusions: AVO fluid factor "may be resolving" hydrocarbon-charged El Abra but forward models show only a subtle brine vs HC difference; calibration needed; inversion limited by complex velocity field; future work: extend fluid factor downdip SE of Tecolutla and prestack inversion to identify/quantify the downdip OWC. Block summary: fields more depleted than expected, missing monthly production data, "inadequate resource to justify even low bid levels".
key_data_with_units: Table "El Abra Seismic Template Summary" (CNIH vs IFR columns): Tecolutla CNIH 3.1 km^2, OOIP 7.8 MMbbl, OGIP 8.8 bcf, Np 1.9 MMbbl, Gp 1.7 bcf, oil RF 24 %, gas RF 20 %; IFR OOIP 26 MMbbl, GOR 515 scf/bbl, solution-gas OGIP 13.4 bcf (no gas cap), oil RF 7 %, gas RF 13 %, remaining oil 7.9 MMbbl. Gutierrez Zamora: CNIH 2.6 MMbbl / IFR 5.0 MMbbl, GOR 515, RF 40 % vs 21 %, remaining 0.85 MMbbl. Miguel Hidalgo: CNIH 38.1 MMbbl / IFR 22.6 MMbbl, GOR 1,100 scf/bbl, sol gas 24.9 + gas cap 4.2 = 29 bcf, IFR oil RF 38 %, gas RF 28 %. Vicente Guerrero: CNIH 13.6 / IFR 6.0 MMbbl, IFR RF 83 % oil, 66 % gas. Text "Oil 33Mbbl", "Oil 61Mbbl" next to "Recent drilling results in Miguel Hidalgo confirm the high recovery factor" (well names/dates not in the text). (file 142XvPwho8KQR8eCEMwDavZh8Id4hLpGI, slide text; the table row cells are shifted by one where a cell is empty, columns assigned by arithmetic check: 1.9/26 = 7.3 %, 26 x 515 scf = 13.4 bcf)
interpretation: Most important: an early IFR volumetric put Tecolutla OOIP at 26 MMbbl (3.3x the CNH 7.8 and 2.3x IFR's later 11.2 MMbbl), with 7.9 MMbbl remaining. The 7.9 reproduces as 26 x ~38 % - 1.9, i.e. the Miguel Hidalgo IFR recovery factor applied to Tecolutla (my arithmetic; the deck does not state the method). This predates TEC-10/TEC-11 results and shows the OOIP has been revised down by more than half; a buyer engineer may see this number elsewhere. IFR GOR 515 scf/bbl for Tecolutla and Gutierrez Zamora is an assumption, not a measurement (G-31 no PVT). The AVO/fluid-factor and MH-412 rock-physics work (10-degree angle stack, PSTM gathers) shows that pre-stack products existed in early 2018, adding to G-55; the deck itself admits brine vs oil carbonate gives only a subtle response. Miguel Hidalgo IFR RF 38 % and the claim that recent MH wells confirm a high RF support the analogue RF range. No aquifer or well-performance data beyond the two unlabelled "Oil 33/61 Mbbl" figures.
use_in_presentation: OOIP history slide (26 -> 11.2 -> P50 10.0 vs CNH 7.8); seismic slide (AVO fluid factor tried, inconclusive); analogue RF slide (Miguel Hidalgo 38 % IFR basis)
repo_impact: adds: earlier IFR OOIP 26 MMbbl not in repo (extends G-41 OOIP reconciliation); adds G-55 (AVOFF volume, angle stacks, PSTM gathers, Vp/Vs rock-physics study existed by 2018-02; none in repo); adds G-31 (515 scf/bbl assumed GOR); contradicts nothing directly, but the 26 MMbbl conflicts with every OOIP the review quotes
